Colin Goodman wrote:

> But saying that, I don't think the G1's are that bad. In fact I'm moving to

> and they work ok.

Group 1's certainly aren't that bad, overall.

-The 2-4's are generally identical to newer vampires (a 2 with 1 discipline;
a 3 with 2 disciplines; a 4 with 3 disciplines or a superior and an
inferior).

-The 5-6's, barring vampires with +1 bleed and +1 strength, are generally
the same as well (i.e. 5's with 2 superiors and an inferior like
Raven/Camille or Felicia Mostrom; 6's with 2 superiors and 2 inferiors like
Badger). Where the G1 5-6's suffer compared to current 5-6's is when they
have special abilities--there is a good handfull of G1 5"s with 4 inferiors
and a sketchy special ability (like, say, Tiberius, Scandalmonger or Sabine
Lafitte) that look weak compared to current designs, and 6's with +1
strength/+1 bleed (look at Zack North and Adrianne and compare them to
similar 6 pointers with the same special abilities) certainly pale in
comparison.

-The 7-8's have one less point of stuff than current 7-8's, which makes a
difference in terms of total disciplines or special abilities, and they
certainly look weak if they have +1 bleed/strength, but still, most of the
G1 7-8's are very solid (see the likes of Selma the Repugnant, Gitaine St.
Claire). Some of the 7-8's seem very weak (like, say, Ebaneezer Roush), but
again, this is uasually due to having +1 strength or bleed.

-The 9-10's in G1, again, lack about 2 points of stuff compared to current
designs, so if you have, like, a 10 point G1 vampire with +1 bleed, say, he
is going to look very soft compared to the G2/G3/G4 10 pointers. But still,
they likely have a home somewhere.

So overall, the only really significantly weak G1 vampires are generally the
9-10 pointers and the vampires with +1 strength or +1 bleed. As long as you
tend to make those G1 vampires the fringe element, you'll never notice that
the G1 vampires have slightly less stuff than the G2+ vampires.

If I thought anyone was interested in coming up with a good point system for
evaluating the power of vampires, I could see the possible value of using
points to argue who should or shouldn't be fixed, but until then, the standard
I'd use is how often the vampire does/should see play.

Does Tura see any more play than Bianca? Doesn't Democritus see at least some
play? - That sort of thing.

BTW, some group 1s probably shouldn't get help unless the game changes in a
dramatic way. The 1/2 vampire pool for Malks is pathetic compared to what it
could be yet Dominate plus stealth (plus P/Js on top of that) is so insanely
powerful that 1/2 Malks still rank high.

>Oh well. They've been re-printed and there's not a lot that can be done
>now.

The fact of the matter is that all CCGs are full of crap, which BTW is
something I put on the heads of design and development. It might be fine to
say "some cards will always be better than other cards" but the more you
tolerate that the more extremes in power you produce.

It's not worth the effort and pain to rehabilitate so many cards. You will
drive the player base freaking crazy by trying. I'm surprised that V:TES has
seen as much rehabilitation as it has. I would have thought trying to figure
out where to draw the line between "we'll fix this" and "we won't bother" would
have prevented most of what has happened. Off the top of my head, Concealed
Weapon is the only one that comes to mind as being an easy choice since it was
always obviously in error rather than just being bad. I, personally, might be
fine with some ass DS card becoming not unplayable, but I don't see how it
helps the game any to add another level of confusion to players who aren't as
familiar with the game. It's just so much easier to print a new card that does
what you wanted the old card to do.

There are a couple of positive ways going forward to make crap better that
don't involve changing cards. The first may or may not end up happening
accidentally; if the metagame shifts, previously weak cards may suddenly become
much more useful. Anachronism, which may still not be so hot but at least gets
talked about for seeing play, would be an example.

This is one of the reasons, if not the primary one, I'd like to see a bit more
drama when new sets come out or whenever. Reevaluating cards for a changed
metagame is kind of like getting new cards.

The other is to come up with new cards/strategies that make better use of old
junk. The anarch option has changed some valuations of older vamps (though,
that it weakens Primogen even more was not a positive benefit).

So, one thing that would be hugely useful is to do something big with Primogen.
Yes, I'd be a bit concerned with the unintended effect of making solid
vampires like Antoinette, Carna, and Tyler better. But, it may be possible to
work around to some degree. I'd look at trying not to help the voting power of
Primogen so much as doing something else for them as I'd be concerned with a
general problem of Primogen with Presence turning into more Princes. And, to a
degree, I'd have a "so what?" attitude towards elevating the better Primogen if
it meant making a lot of other cards good enough to see play. "Some cards will
always be better than others" cuts both ways - having not suck Primogen
suddenly be better than [blank] is interesting simply because [blank] is *no
longer* the best thing going. And, if you aid *everything* underpowered
eventually, maybe you move to a greater total balance in the long run.

Well, this is that silly semantic argument that results in endless
discussions about Ian Forrestal.

The fact of the matter is, yes, Anvil has too much stuff compared to most
other 6 point vampires (the vast majority of 6 point vampires in the old set
and the new set and all the middle sets have 6 points of stuff, where each
level of a discipline is worth 1 point, and other abilities are worth
something tomake up the difference). Anvil has, what, 7 points in
disciplines and a vote, equalling about 7.5 points of stuff on a vampire
that should have, compared to all of his classmates, 6 points of stuff.

Does this make him "too powerful" in the sense that using him will
automatically make you win games? No. But it does make him "too powerful" in
the sense that he has too much stuff for his cost, much like Ian Forrestal,
and in the same sense that Zack North is "underpowered"--using Zack North
isn't going to make you *lose*games. Heck, you could win games all the time
with Zack North in play with the appropriate deck. But he is still weak
compared to his classmates--he should have, like, an extra superior
discipline or something to make him the appropriate.

If you are willing to accept that some vampires are "too weak" (i.e. don't
get enough stuff for their cost--see Judah; Adrianne), then you need to
accept that some vampires are "too strong". This doesn't mean that these
vampires make you automatically win the game (due to the structure of the
game). But it does mean that they are outside of the bounds of the
established design system, and probably shouldn't be.

This being said, I don't think it was particularly necessary to fix the G1
vampires, as most of them are fine. I mean, yeah, it would have been nice to
see Zack North get PRO, Adrianne get PRE, Ebazeezer get POT, and Democritus
get FOR. But that they didn't isn't that big of a deal in the long run, as
still, most of the vampires are within the bounds of standard design.

"Curevei" <cur...@aol.commetal> wrote

> last is
> very messy, I think, to incorporate into a point system.

I have, in the past, used my own point system. It's fairly arbitrary, and in
fact has to be arbitrary because it is based around each unique deck that I
make.

What I do is assign values based on what I want a particular deck to do. So,
let's say I want to make a Lasombra with Presence deck. Obviously, Lasombras
with Presence are going to value higher than those without. Since it is a
votey deck, vampires with titles will value higher than those that do not.
Gratiano will get more points than Tobias, even though Tobias has all the
requisite disciplines at superior.

I think we all do this mentally when we make a deck, but I don't know too
many players that write it out like I often do.

So, the official point system may make sense for designing vampires but it
makes no sense to apply the same formula when designing a deck. If I was
building a deck around [CHI/aus/pot] then Tereza Rostas would not suck...
she would be ideal. (Of course, the deck itself might suck, but that's
beside the point.)

The official point system will give someone like Harrod a lot of points,
based on the extra disciplines, but how useful are those disciplines in any
given deck? How often have you used Arika's [aus]? When a high capacity
vampire has disciplines outside of its clan, those disciplines will
generally only be useful if you are building a deck around that vampire and
its unique discipline spread. My decks based around Howler (and there have
been a lot of them) always have one or two Obfuscate cards (usually Hidden
Lurker). But if you weren't using her [obf], how much is it worth?

Because of this, I feel that a lot of the larger vampires are getting
shortchanged. Take Zayyat for example. I don't know offhand how much he
would be worth according to the current design system, but I assume that he
fits the template. But how useful is [aus/qui/tha] really? I would much
rather have just [AUS] or just [THA]. (I'll pass on [QUI], thank you.) The
design system may give him an appropriate cost, but he is effectively
useless because his disciplines are all over the place. So my personal
system would consider him a fairly shitty vampire in most decks.

Other vampires who have a superior discipline outside of their clan are
valued much higher by most people I know, because they can have interesting
decks built around them. Moncada and Polonia both have [PRE]. Arika's [OBF]
is always useful etc. I agree with Curevei that superior is much more
valuable than the point system makes it out to be. And an off-clan superior
is even more valuable, for the decks it makes possible.

Overall, I would disagree that the official design system is flawed,
exactly. Rather, it is useless for us end users trying to make a deck.

Cheers,
WES

As I've been reading through this thread, I keep thinking that it
should be obvious that a mistake was made when some of the G1 vampires
weren't improved in some way. Even if only a handful of them had been
"upgraded" with a superior discipline that they had in inferior (or
whatever else would have made them more playable), then we all would
have benefited from it.

The players would be happy because there would be a few more useful
vampires that were mostly regarded as wallpaper for the last several
years.

The sales probably would have gone up for the set, so the folks at
White Wolf would have been pleased with that outcome. I certainly
would be much more interested in these anniversary sets if some of the
vampires were "fixed" instead of being the same old useless junk they
have been for years.

And even the collectors might have been pleased because their original
vamps would have been even more unique. Of course, I don't know much
about how the collectors think... Are their collectors in this
newsgroup who can answer that question? Would you guys have been ok
with such changes?

The more I think about it, I simply can't understand why anyone at
White Wolf would sanction the reprinting of cards or vamps that are
considered to be wallpaper by most people. A little tweaking here and
there could have gone a long way to make these two sets a LOT more
interesting.

Isn't there a middle ground between making a few small improvements and
reworking almost all of the G1 vampires? I think that choosing the
most obviously bad vampires and making a few minor changes would have
left everyone fairly satisfied with the results. Even if it was only
5-10 vamps, that could have caused quite a stir of excitement within
most playgroups.

Personally, I hope that the people at White Wolf will hear the
complaints and comments of everyone that is talking about the
anniversary sets and make some adjustments to any sets they print in
the future. I like the idea of "fixing" a few cards here and there...
it certainly breaths new life into cards that have been shelved or are
being used as drink coasters or bookmarks.

So my personal request goes something like this...

- Smaller expansions, more often

- Fix some of the reprints that have obvious problems

- Create advanced versions of G1 vamps that are truly useful

- Continue to listen to the players for ideas and suggestions (as you
have in the past)

...and keep making the game fun and interesting for all the new players
and old players alike, without suddenly rocking the boat so much that
people quit and walk away from the game or split off into separate
groups.

Just a few thoughts from someone who is currently on the sidelines...
Cheers,
Howard
